messages:
ben: Hey team — customer on prod reporting intermittent 401s after we rotated their API key yesterday. Error only affects some requests, roughly 5-10%.
alice: Thanks Ben. Any pattern on which hosts or endpoints? Is it across all routes or only generation calls?
ben: They say it’s mostly long-running background jobs (Celery/gunicorn) hitting the text-generation endpoint. Frontend requests seem fine.
carol: Do we have logs? Can you paste a sample request/response (redact keys) and pod/worker id?
ben: Pasted log:

```
INFO Request id=abc123 worker=web-2 POST /v1/generate 401 Unauthorized
resp: {"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"Authentication failed"}
headers: {"Authorization":"Bearer <REDACTED>", "X-Redwood-Org":"org_foo"}
```

Note: same request a few seconds later from a different worker succeeds.
alice: That smells like per-process env caching. What’s the deployment? Gunicorn config? Preload app?
ben: They use gunicorn with preload_app = True and 4 workers. Gunicorn conf snippet:

```
preload_app = True
workers = 4
timeout = 120
```

dave: If preload_app is true, module imports happen in master and get copied to workers. If the SDK reads REDWOOD_API_KEY at import time into a module-global, workers will hold stale key until restart.
carol: Does our python SDK cache the key on import? I thought we read os.environ in the Client constructor, but some apps build a global client at import time (client = RedwoodClient()) and never recreate it.
alice: Two possible causes:
- app creates a global client object at module import and gunicorn preload copies that into workers -> they all keep old key
- SDK itself might cache env at import time (older SDK versions had a module-level DEFAULT_API_KEY = os.getenv(...))

Which SDK version is the customer on?
ben: v1.2.0
alice: OK. v1.2.0 had a known issue where DEFAULT_AUTH was evaluated at import time (see internal changelog). We fixed it in v1.3.1 to defer reading env until the Client instance is created and also added a refresh hook.
carol: Workarounds until they can upgrade:
- Restart all worker processes after key rotation (quick but disruptive)
- Ensure app does NOT instantiate a global client at import time; construct client inside request/worker start code
- Pass explicit api_key to Client constructor pulled from a file/secret provider that can be re-read per request

ben: Customer needs a non-disruptive mitigation — they can’t restart all workers during business hours.
alice: Another practical workaround: set preload_app = False (causes workers to read env at fork time rather than copying preloaded objects) or change gunicorn config to re-exec workers on SIGHUP when rotation occurs.
dave: For long-term, recommend upgrading to >= v1.3.1 which includes:
- per-request credential resolution
- Client.refresh_auth() API
- creds provider callback: Client(api_key_provider=lambda: open('/etc/creds/redwood.key').read().strip())

Example provider pattern:

```
from redwood import RedwoodClient

def file_provider():
    with open('/etc/creds/redwood.key') as f:
        return f.read().strip()

client = RedwoodClient(api_key_provider=file_provider)
```

This avoids env caching and works across rotation without process restarts.
carol: Also call out org/project header handling — if they relied on REDWOOD_ORG env and SDK defaulted to reading that once, same problem. Recommend passing org explicitly when creating client or via provider.
ben: I sent the above to customer and asked which mitigation they prefer. They asked for a quick test to confirm the cause.
alice: Ask them to temporarily run one worker with preload_app=False or spawn a fresh worker with the new key and see if that worker succeeds while old ones fail. That will confirm the preload/import-time caching hypothesis.
ben: Will do. Also opened a ticket to prioritize a support doc about key rotation with common server patterns (gunicorn, celery, uvicorn reloads).
deploy-bot: NOTE: internal SDK PR #842 fixed env-caching on import; patch included in release v1.3.1. :white_check_mark:
carol: Thanks. Post back results and we’ll follow up with upgrade instructions and a KB article snippet. :thumbsup:
